title: How to Handle Background Noise When Using Conversation Relay in Node.js
summary: This tutorial walks you through choosing the right Deepgram speech model for noisy conditions in a Twilio Conversation Relay agent, and shows you which TwiML attributes to tune when the defaults fall short.
body_text: Time to read: July 23, 2026 Written by Dylan Frankcom Twilion Dhruv Patel Twilion How to Handle Background Noise When Using Conversation Relay in Node.js Background noise is one of the most common real-world failure modes for voice AI agents. When your speech-to-text model mishears a caller, the entire response chain breaks down from that first bad transcript. This tutorial walks you through choosing the right Deepgram speech model for noisy conditions in a Twilio Conversation Relay agent, and shows you which TwiML (Twilio Markup Language) attributes to tune when the defaults fall short. Prerequisites To follow this tutorial you will need: The Owl Air phone agent from the previous tutorial, or any Conversation Relay agent built with Node.js and Express A voice-capable Twilio phone number ngrok running and your DOMAIN environment variable set How background noise affects voice AI Before tuning anything, it helps to understand exactly where noise causes issues. When a human call center agent hears a noisy caller, they can ask for clarification or piece together meaning from context. A voice AI agent cannot do this. It processes a chain of three sequential steps, and noise corrupts the very first one. The chain looks like this: the caller speaks, Deepgram converts that speech to text (STT), your server passes the text to the language model (LLM), the model replies in text, and ElevenLabs converts the reply to speech (TTS). If background noise causes Deepgram to transcribe something incorrectly, that error is what reaches the LLM. The model has no audio to fall back on. It can only work with what the transcript says. The result could be a confused or nonsensical response. All the leverage is at that first step. If the STT transcript is accurate, the rest of the chain works correctly regardless of what the caller's environment sounds like. Testing methodology To get concrete findings rather than speculation, the testing covered four conditions on speakerphone at arm's length: no noise (quiet room baseline), a vacuum cleaner (~70 to 75 dB at one metre), an intermittent power drill (~85 to 90 dB), and both running simultaneously. Nova-2 was also evaluated briefly at the outset and ruled out. It underperformed Nova-3 even in the quiet baseline picking up audio from a podcast playing quietly on a nearby speaker, so it wasn't carried forward into the noise conditions. Three configurations made it through the full testing suite: the baseline Deepgram Nova-3 config from the previous tutorial; a tuned Nova-3 config with the attribute changes described later in this post; and Deepgram Flux on its default configuration. Each call followed a six-exchange script covering policy questions, flight number lookups, number transcription, low-information input, incomplete phrases, and deliberate interruptions. The terminal logged transcripts via the CALLER: log lines. A failure counted when Deepgram's output differed meaningfully from what was said in a way that changed the agent's response. All three configurations handled single-noise conditions without issue. The gap only showed up under combined noise: default Nova-3 produced two transcription failures, while tuned Nova-3 and Flux both passed cleanly. Model configuration Nova-3 The previous tutorial used nova-3-general . Nova-3 handles single-noise conditions cleanly. The default config does break under worst-case combined noise, however. Two exchanges failed: Deepgram transcribed "Can you explain the loyalty points program in detail" as "Can you explain the loyalty forms program in detail", and "What's the check-in window?" came through as "What's the second window?". Two attribute changes brought the error count to zero. Reducing false interruptions interruptSensitivity controls how easily background sound can interrupt Hoot mid-response. The previous tutorial used medium . In a noisy environment, medium sensitivity can cause Hoot to stop speaking every time a noise spike crosses the detection threshold. Setting it to low raises that threshold so only deliberate speech interrupts the agent: Copy code interruptSensitivity="low", The tradeoff is that a caller who genuinely wants to interrupt will need to speak a little more deliberately. For most support calls, that is a reasonable price for an agent that does not stop mid-sentence every time a power tool runs nearby. Suppressing backchannel responses ignoreBackchannel controls whether Conversation Relay responds when a caller makes a brief affirmative sound while Hoot is actively speaking. Sounds like "uh huh", "yeah", or "mm" signal the caller is listening rather than taking a turn. When set to true , those sounds are ignored and Hoot continues without treating them as a new prompt: Copy code ignoreBackchannel="true", This setting is distinct from interruptSensitivity . interruptSensitivity governs whether any sound stops Hoot mid-sentence. ignoreBackchannel governs whether a recognised backchannel triggers a response once Hoot has finished speaking. You typically want both in a noisy environment: interruptSensitivity="low" to prevent noise spikes from cutting Hoot off, and ignoreBackchannel="true" to prevent a caller's "uh huh" from generating an unnecessary reply. ignoreBackchannel only applies while Hoot is talking. A caller saying "yeah" as a standalone turn after Hoot has finished is a legitimate prompt, and the agent will respond to it regardless of this setting. Nova-3 endpoint configuration Here is the full /twiml endpoint with both attribute changes applied: Copy code app.post('/twiml', (req, res) => { const domain = process.env.DOMAIN || ''; const twiml = ` <Response> <Connect> <ConversationRelay url="wss://\${domain}/ws" welcomeGreeting="Thanks for calling Owl Air! I'm Hoot. I can help with flight status, baggage policy, loyalty points, or booking changes. Which of those can I help you with?" ttsProvider="ElevenLabs" transcriptionProvider="Deepgram" speechModel="nova-3-general" ignoreBackchannel="true" hints="Owl Air, loyalty points, baggage, carry-on, check-in, boarding pass" interruptible="any" interruptSensitivity="low" elevenlabsTextNormalization="auto" /> </Connect> </Response> `; res.type('application/xml'); res.send(twiml); }); The changes from the previous tutorial are ignoreBackchannel set to true and interruptSensitivity changed from medium to low . No other code in index.js changes. Flux Flux support was recently added to Conversation Relay and is the better option for any agent that can adopt it. It passed all four noise conditions on its default config, including the worst-case combined condition, without any additional configuration. Beyond noise handling, it fuses transcription and turns detection into a single model. This eliminates the race conditions that cause agents to cut callers off mid-sentence, reduces response latency by 200 to 600ms, and cuts false interruptions by roughly 30 percent compared to Nova-3. It also adds native multilingual support across ten languages. See Deepgram's Flux announcement for the full breakdown. To use it, update speechModel in your /twiml endpoint: Copy code speechModel="flux", Both interruptSensitivity and ignoreBackchannel are available on Flux as well if you want additional hardening on top of the defaults. Tuning end-of-turn detection Flux performed well across all noise conditions during testing without any additional tuning. If you are in an exceptionally loud environment and still seeing turn detection misfiring, Flux exposes eotThreshold as an additional dial. It controls how confident the end-of-turn (EOT) detector must be before finalising a transcript and defaults to 0.8 . Lowering it to 0.75 tells the detector to fire on reasonable confidence, rather than waiting for a certainty level that sustained noise may prevent it from reaching. Try not to go below 0.7 , as lower values risk cutting off callers who speak slowly or pause mid-sentence. This attribute is not available on Nova-3. Copy code eotThreshold=0.75, Flux endpoint configuration If you are upgrading to Flux, the only change is speechModel . The interruptSensitivity and ignoreBackchannel attributes are kept as additional hardening but are not required for Flux to pass the noise conditions tested here: Copy code app.post('/twiml', (req, res) => { const domain = process.env.DOMAIN || ''; const twiml = ` <Response> <Connect> <ConversationRelay url="wss://\${domain}/ws" welcomeGreeting="Thanks for calling Owl Air! I'm Hoot. I can help with flight status, baggage policy, loyalty points, or booking changes. Which of those can I help you with?" ttsProvider="ElevenLabs" transcriptionProvider="Deepgram" speechModel="flux" ignoreBackchannel="true" hints="Owl Air, loyalty points, baggage, carry-on, check-in, boarding pass" interruptible="any" interruptSensitivity="low" elevenlabsTextNormalization="auto" /> </Connect> </Response> `; res.type('application/xml'); res.send(twiml); }); If you are on Flux and still seeing turn detection misfiring after that, try lowering eotThreshold to 0.75 . Preprocessing audio Audio preprocessing libraries like ElevenLabs Audio Isolation API are designed for offline processing and are not compatible with a Conversation Relay pipeline. The core constraint is that your server never receives raw caller audio. Twilio routes inbound audio directly to Deepgram for transcription, and your server only receives JSON messages containing the finished transcript. There is no point in that path where you can intercept audio, clean it, and forward the result. ElevenLabs Audio Isolation has a similar limitation. It processes audio files you upload and is only involved on the outbound side in a Conversation Relay call, converting text responses to speech. It has no role in the inbound audio path. Twilio's <Stream> verb can fork raw audio to your server, but it cannot run alongside <ConversationRelay> . <ConversationRelay> takes full ownership of the call's media pipeline, and <Stream> blocks subsequent TwiML execution once it connects. Using audio preprocessing libraries in a Twilio pipeline would require replacing Conversation Relay entirely with a custom Media Streams architecture: your own STT, LLM, and TTS with audio preprocessing in the middle. That is a significantly larger project and introduces latency at every additional hop. Conclusion Talking on speakerphone while simultaneously running a vacuum cleaner and a power drill is most likely a rare occurrence, but it did produce a clear answer. Flux handled all four noise conditions on its default config without any additional changes. For agents that cannot move to Flux yet, Nova-3 with interruptSensitivity="low" and ignoreBackchannel="true" brings it to zero failures under the same worst-case conditions. See the Conversation Relay documentation for the full attribute reference. Dhruv Patel is a Developer on Twilio's Developer Voices team. You can find Dhruv working in a coffee shop with a glass of cold brew or he can be reached at dhrpatel [at] twilio.com .

title: Beanonomics: $BEAN Flows in the Peg Mechanism & DAO
summary: An explanation of how Beanstalk's peg mechanism and DAO work
body_text: Last week we talked about Beanstalk’s strengths and weaknesses within the stablecoin trilemma . Price stability is the most difficult aspect of stablecoin design when it comes to algorithmic models, so this week we’re going into much further detail about the mechanisms involved in peg maintenance, as well as other economic forces in the Beanstalk ecosystem. Summarizing the Trilemma Discussion In order for cryptocurrencies to work as money, volatility has to be minimized. The current most popular implementations are stablecoins like USDC and USDT, which achieve stability by holding reserve assets equivalent to the amount of tokens issued. However, this design falls short on the axes of decentralization and capital efficiency. Beanstalk is an experiment that attempts to algorithmically balance $BEAN supply and demand in order to achieve price stability, doing so in a decentralized and highly capital efficient manner. The tradeoff with this system is an increased likelihood of volatility due to dependence on the participation of creditors who will lend their $BEAN to the protocol. How Beanstalk Incentivizes Supply & Demand Balance In order to return the price to $1 when $BEAN is below peg, Beanstalk attempts to reduce the supply by adjusting the interest rate ( Temperature ) for lending to the protocol. When $BEAN is lent to Beanstalk ( Sown ) it is burned, taking supply off the market. Lending is done through Beanstalk’s credit facility, the Field . When $BEAN holders lend they receive Pods , which can be Harvested for $BEAN in the future. $BEAN loans have no set duration, and Pods become Harvestable on a first-in, first-out basis. The current Temperature determines how many Pods the lender will receive per $BEAN loaned, and thus how many $BEANs can be Harvested upon reaching the front of the first-in first-out Pod Line . The Temperature is the interest rate for lending $BEAN and it is adjusted at the beginning of each Season (~1 hour period). The Beanstalk algorithm alters the Temperature based on the amount of lending happening in an attempt to converge the price to $1. In addition to changing the Temperature , Beanstalk algorithmically adjusts the available supply of Soil , which is the amount of $BEAN the protocol is willing to borrow. The protocol is always willing to borrow, but the amount changes based on the amount of liquidity as well as the excess or shortage of $BEAN in the liquidity pools used as price oracles. Soil supply is also adjusted at the beginning of each Season in order to help converge $BEAN price to $1. Quick peg explanation to give context to the section above: $BEAN is pegged to $1, but how does Beanstalk determine where price is in relation to the peg? It uses the BEAN:3CRV pool on Curve as an oracle. The pool contains $BEAN and 3CRV, an LP token for the 3pool, which contains 3 of the most commonly used stablecoins; $USDC, $USDT, and $DAI. If the ratio of $BEAN value to 3CRV value in the pool is 50:50, then $BEAN is considered to be at its intended peg. When the $BEAN price is greater than $1 the Temperature is lowered, resulting in less Pods received per $BEAN loaned. As more Pods become harvestable and get redeemed for $BEAN, combined with lending to the protocol becoming less attractive, the supply should rise relative to demand, providing downwards price pressure to push $BEAN back down towards the peg. This constitutes the basis of Beanstalk’s peg mechanism, Soil supply and Temperature are adjustable. This means the protocol can adapt the amount of debt it needs to offer, and the interest rate associated with new debt, with a goal of influencing the market supply and then ultimately the price. If you are interested in a more granular view into how Beanstalk adjusts these parameters please see the Field section of the docs, as well as the whitepaper . If you’re more of a visual learner check out the graphic below. The Role of the Beanstalk DAO Besides lending $BEAN to Beanstalk through the Field , the other main way to participate in the growth of the protocol is depositing $BEAN in the Silo . Depositing in the Silo stakes a holder’s $BEAN, in exchange rewarding them with Stalk and Seed tokens. Stalk is a governance token, used to create and vote on Beanstalk Improvement Proposals (BIPs). Seed tokens generate Stalk over time, at a rate of 1/10000 per Season. With Seasons lasting approximately 1 hour, each Seed will generate 1 full Stalk every 416 days. Additionally, Stalkholders are entitled to seigniorage, which rewards them with 1/3rd of new $BEAN supply that is minted through the Field . In addition to $BEAN, BEAN:3CRVLP tokens and Unripe Assets can also be deposited in the Silo. LP tokens grant additional Seed rewards to incentivize liquidity for $BEAN. The purpose of Silo deposits receiving these rewards is to provide protocol-native utility for $BEAN, giving people an incentive to hold it so they can earn seigniorage and participate in governance. Demand for $BEAN is ultimately the driving force that allows the peg mechanisms discussed above to function. While the peg system’s design gives $BEAN innate utility, as it can be Sown to later mint new $BEAN plus interest, giving holders more venues to use $BEAN will help strengthen demand and make the system run more smoothly. This concept is an important part of upcoming items on the roadmap for Beanstalk, which includes restoring on-chain governance and developing new $BEAN trading pairs. Unripe Assets Unripe Assets were mentioned in the previous section as eligible for deposit in the Silo , so let’s explain what purpose they serve within the ecosystem. In April 2022 Beanstalk suffered a governance exploit, which drained ~$77M worth of assets from the Silo . In an effort to recapitalize the lost funds the DAO created the Barn, as well as Fertilizer and Sprouts . Fertilizer is an ERC-1155 token that can be bought for 1 USDC, and comes with an associated number of Sprouts. At the outset of this recapitalization program Fertilizer supply was at 77M, available fertilizer supply fluctuates based on sales and unripe BEAN3CRV conversions. The USDC taken in from Fertilizer sales serves to deepen liquidity in the BEAN 3crv pool. As new $BEAN is minted through the peg mechanism described in section 1 of this piece, Sprouts become Rinsable Sprouts, meaning that they can be redeemed for $BEAN. 1/3rd of newly minted $BEAN goes towards this process. Unripe Assets are another part of the Barn . An equivalent amount of these were awarded to everyone who held $BEAN or whitelisted LP tokens at the time of the exploit. Unripe $BEAN and Unripe Bean:3CRV represent a pro rata claim on the underlying Ripe $BEAN and Ripe Bean:3CRV that is minted when Fertilizer is sold. Summing it Up Beanstalk is no doubt a complex system, however, it’s an attempt at making significant progress in the stablecoin trilemma, and ambitious goals often require ambitious designs. Hopefully this explanation gave you a better understanding of Beanstalk’s experimental economic design, and how the peg mechanism, DAO, and recapitalization effort are all tied together. As always, the Farmers over on Discord are an excellent resource for any questions about Beanstalk, and our new Twitter account is coming out with fresh educational threads and organic Bean memes all the time. Blog posts will be regularly scheduled now, coming out every Monday, so check in next week for an analysis of Beanstalk’s Q1 ‘23 metrics.

title: 🔒 Cómo proteger tu información y evitar el robo de identidad
summary: Cada vez usamos más nuestro celular para hacer trámites, pedir un préstamo, comprar o hacer pagos. Por eso, proteger tu información personal es más importante que nunca. Si alguien obtiene tus datos y los usa sin tu permiso, podría hacerse pasar por ti para solicitar un crédito, acceder a tus
body_text: Cada vez usamos más nuestro celular para hacer trámites, pedir un préstamo, comprar o hacer pagos. Por eso, proteger tu información personal es más importante que nunca. Si alguien obtiene tus datos y los usa sin tu permiso, podría hacerse pasar por ti para solicitar un crédito, acceder a tus cuentas o realizar otros trámites en tu nombre. La buena noticia es que hay formas muy sencillas de reducir ese riesgo y actuar rápidamente si llegara a suceder. 🤔 ¿Qué significa el robo de identidad? El robo de identidad ocurre cuando alguien obtiene información personal como tu nombre, CURP, INE, número de celular, correo electrónico o datos bancarios para hacerse pasar por ti. Con esa información pueden intentar solicitar créditos, hacer compras o acceder a cuentas sin tu autorización. Por eso es importante proteger tus datos y estar atento a cualquier actividad que no reconozcas. ⚠️ ¿Cómo pueden robar tu información? Muchas veces pensamos que el robo de identidad solo ocurre cuando hackean una cuenta, pero en realidad puede pasar de formas muy comunes. Algunos ejemplos son: Recibes un mensaje o correo que parece ser de una empresa y te pide ingresar tus datos en una página falsa. Alguien te llama haciéndose pasar por un banco o una institución y te pide códigos de verificación o información personal. Compartes datos personales en redes sociales o con personas que no conoces. Pierdes tu celular y no tiene bloqueo de pantalla o contraseña. Utilizas contraseñas muy fáciles de adivinar o la misma contraseña en varias cuentas. La mejor forma de protegerte es desconfiar de cualquier persona o sitio que te pida información personal si no estás completamente seguro de que es un canal oficial. 🛡️ ¿Cómo puedes prevenir el robo de identidad? No existe una forma de evitarlo al 100%, pero sí puedes reducir mucho el riesgo siguiendo estas recomendaciones. ✅ Mantén tus datos de contacto actualizados No esperes a que Baubap te solicite actualizar tu información. Si cambias de número de celular, correo electrónico, domicilio o cuenta bancaria, recuerda actualizar esos datos también en tu app de Baubap lo antes posible. Es muy sencillo: Inicia sesión en tu app de Baubap. Selecciona “Perfil” en la parte inferior derecha. Modifica la información que necesites actualizar, como tu número telefónico, domicilio, CLABE bancaria o cualquier otro dato disponible. Mantener tu información al día nos ayuda a comunicarnos contigo y a proteger mejor tu cuenta ante cualquier actividad inusual. 🔐 Cambia tu NIP cada 3 meses Cambiar tu NIP periódicamente es una forma sencilla de proteger tu cuenta. Te recomendamos actualizarlo al menos cada 3 meses . Además: Evita usar fechas de nacimiento o números fáciles de adivinar. No compartas tu NIP ni tus contraseñas con nadie. Si utilizas otras cuentas, procura que cada una tenga una contraseña diferente. 📩 Pon atención a los correos de inicio de sesión Muchas aplicaciones y servicios envían un correo o una notificación cuando detectan un inicio de sesión desde un dispositivo nuevo. Si recibes uno y tú no fuiste, actúa de inmediato: Cambia tu contraseña. Cierra la sesión en todos tus dispositivos, si la plataforma lo permite. Contacta a soporte escribiendo a soporte@baubap.com . Mientras más rápido actúes, menor será el riesgo. 📄 Revisa tu Buró de Crédito cada mes Una buena práctica es revisar tu Buró de Crédito al menos una vez al mes. Así podrás detectar si aparece algún crédito o movimiento que no reconoces y actuar antes de que el problema crezca. 🚨 ¿Qué hacer si sospechas que alguien robó tu información? Si notas movimientos extraños o crees que alguien está usando tus datos, no esperes. Actuar rápido puede ayudarte a evitar mayores problemas. Te recomendamos seguir estos pasos: Cambia inmediatamente las contraseñas y el NIP de tus cuentas. Contacta a la institución donde detectaste el movimiento para reportar el caso. Revisa tu Buró de Crédito para verificar si existe algún crédito que no solicitaste. Conserva cualquier correo, mensaje o evidencia que pueda ayudar durante la investigación. Si confirmas que hubo un robo de identidad, presenta una denuncia ante las autoridades correspondientes. 🙌 Proteger tu información también protege tu tranquilidad Así como cuidas tu dinero, también es importante cuidar tu información personal. Actualizar tus datos de contacto, cambiar tu NIP cada tres meses, revisar tu Buró de Crédito y poner atención a las alertas de inicio de sesión son acciones sencillas que pueden ayudarte a prevenir el robo de identidad. En Baubap trabajamos para proteger tu información, pero recuerda que la seguridad también empieza contigo. ¿Necesitas ayuda o detectaste alguna actividad que no reconoces en tu cuenta? Ponte en contacto con nosotros a través de nuestros canales oficiales. Evita Fraudes: Nuestros Medios Oficiales de contacto Asegúrate de usar nuestros canales oficiales para evitar estafas. Distribution & Warehousing Associations: Which Should You Join?
summary: If you’ve been looking to connect with other professionals in the distribution and warehousing industry, there’s no shortage of groups to join. In this post, we break down some of the top associations by location, who they’re best for, and the resources they offer to members.
body_text: If you’ve been looking to connect with other professionals in the distribution and warehousing industry, there’s no shortage of groups to join. In this post, we break down some of the top associations by location, who they’re best for, and the resources they offer to members. In no particular order: International Warehouse Logistics Association (IWLA) Location : North America Who should join? Third-Party Logistics (3PL) companies What resources do they offer? Annual IWLA Convention & Expo, workshops, seminars, an insurance captive, networking, warehouse law, retained counsel services, warehouse forms, promotion of the 3PL industry, and a warehouse directory ‍ Warehouse Education and Resource Council (WERC) ‍ Location : United States Who should join? All warehousing and distribution professionals What resources do they offer? body_text: HOUSTON, Feb. 3, 2025 /PRNewswire/ — Noble Corporation plc (“Noble” or the “Company”) (NYSE: NE) today announces plans to divest the cold stacked drillships Pacific Meltem and Pacific Scirocco in order to eliminate costs related to these units and prioritize resources on the existing marketed fleet. The Company intends to divest these units in a manner which would effectively retire them permanently from drilling operation, including potentially scrapping the units. Robert W. Eifler, President and Chief Executive Officer of Noble Corporation plc, stated, “Our decision to retire these non-contributing assets is based on a continuous cost-benefit evaluation of idle capacity. These retirements will be immediately cash flow accretive and result in a leaner, fitter fleet composition for Noble going forward.” About Noble Corporation Noble is a leading offshore drilling contractor for the oil and gas industry. The Company owns and operates one of the most modern, versatile, and technically advanced fleets in the offshore drilling industry. Noble and its predecessors have been engaged in the contract drilling of oil and gas wells since 1921. Noble performs, through its subsidiaries, contract drilling services with a fleet of offshore drilling units focused largely on ultra-deepwater and high specification jackup drilling opportunities in both established and emerging regions worldwide. title: Best Card Payment Gateways in Singapore (2026): HitPay vs Stripe vs Adyen vs Airwallex
summary: Compare card payment gateways in Singapore — HitPay, Stripe, Adyen, Airwallex, and more. See fees, local e-wallet support, and payout speeds for SG SMBs.
body_text: Quick Answer: HitPay is a MAS-licensed payment gateway (PS20200643) that supports card payments (Visa, Mastercard, Amex, UnionPay, Apple Pay, Google Pay) alongside PayNow, GrabPay, ShopeePay, Atome, and 50+ other payment methods — with no monthly fees and next business day SGD payouts. Singapore SMBs that need both card acceptance and local e-wallets in a single integration will find HitPay the most comprehensive option without a subscription cost. Accepting card payments in Singapore is no longer a differentiator — it is a baseline expectation. Visa and Mastercard are accepted everywhere from Orchard Road boutiques to Tanjong Pagar F&B operators. The real question for SMBs is which gateway delivers card acceptance alongside PayNow, GrabPay, and ShopeePay — without a monthly fee eating into thin margins. Payment gateways operating in Singapore must hold a valid licence from the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) under the Payment Services Act 2019. Choosing an unlicensed provider creates regulatory and financial risk. Every gateway in this comparison is MAS-licensed or operates under a regulated entity. For a broader view of how card payments fit within a full digital payment strategy, the guide to credit card payment options for small businesses in Southeast Asia covers card economics, chargeback risk, and acceptance infrastructure in detail. What card payment methods does each Singapore gateway support? All major gateways in this comparison accept Visa and Mastercard. The differences emerge around Amex, UnionPay, Apple Pay, Google Pay, and — critically for Singapore — local e-wallets and PayNow. Gateway Visa / Mastercard Amex Apple Pay / Google Pay PayNow GrabPay ShopeePay Monthly Fee HitPay ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ $0 Stripe ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌ $0 Adyen ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌ (SG) ❌ (SG) ❌ $0 (per-transaction) Airwallex ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌ ❌ ❌ From $0 (Explore) / $79+ 2C2P ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌ ❌ ❌ Not disclosed PayPal ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌ ❌ ❌ $0 Fiuu ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌ ❌ ❌ Not disclosed Card-only acceptance is sufficient for some use cases — but a Bugis street-wear brand or a Tiong Bahru café that only accepts cards will miss the significant share of Singapore consumers who default to PayNow or GrabPay at checkout. How do payout speeds compare for Singapore card transactions? Cash flow timing is a material operational factor, not an administrative detail. A retail operator waiting T+3 to settle card revenue is effectively extending interest-free credit to their payment provider. HitPay: Next business day in SGD for domestic card and PayNow transactions. Cross-border payments (e.g. WeChatPay, UPI, PromptPay) settle at T+2. Stripe: Standard payout schedule applies; faster payouts available for eligible accounts via debit card. Adyen: “Faster payouts” — exact timing varies by configuration and account tier. 2C2P: T+1 to T+3 depending on payment type. Airwallex / PayPal / Fiuu: Payout timelines vary; merchants should confirm directly. For Singapore SMBs running tight weekly cash cycles, next business day settlement on card revenue is a concrete operational advantage. Which gateways are built for Singapore SMBs vs. enterprise? HitPay Best for: SMBs across Singapore that want card payments, PayNow, GrabPay, ShopeePay, Atome, ShopBack PayLater, and 50+ methods in one integration — with zero monthly fees and next business day SGD payouts. HitPay is MAS-licensed (PS20200643), free to sign up, and approved in 1–3 business days. It also supports cross-border card-adjacent methods including WeChat Pay, UPI (for Indian tourists), QRIS (Indonesian visitors), and PromptPay (Thai visitors) — relevant for merchants in tourist-heavy areas like Orchard Road or Marina Bay. For card transaction pricing, see hitpayapp.com/pricing . The online payment methods available in Singapore guide outlines how these methods work together at checkout. Stripe Best for: Developer-led teams that need extensive API customisation, subscription billing infrastructure, or complex platform payment flows — and can manage ShopeePay’s absence from Stripe’s Singapore method set. Stripe supports PayNow and GrabPay in Singapore alongside full card acceptance including Amex, Apple Pay, and Google Pay. It has no monthly fee. However, ShopeePay is not available as a Stripe payment method in Singapore, and Stripe’s self-serve setup favours technically capable teams over non-technical merchants. Adyen Best for: Enterprise retailers with high transaction volumes, existing Adyen commercial relationships, and dedicated technical teams — not SMBs needing rapid onboarding or local e-wallet support in Singapore. Adyen processes €1.4 trillion annually and maintains 99.999% historical uptime. In Singapore, its documented payment methods are card-focused. PayNow and GrabPay are not listed as supported Singapore methods in available documentation. Onboarding timelines and minimum volume thresholds make Adyen impractical for most SMBs. Airwallex Best for: Businesses that primarily need multi-currency accounts, global FX transfers, and corporate cards — and for whom Singapore local e-wallet acceptance is secondary to treasury management. Airwallex offers strong FX infrastructure and multi-currency corporate cards. Its Grow plan starts at $79/month, and the Accelerate plan from $399/month. For SMBs whose core need is accepting card payments from Singapore consumers alongside PayNow, those subscription fees add meaningful fixed cost without a corresponding local payments advantage. 2C2P Best for: Enterprises operating across Southeast Asia that need over-the-counter payment networks (600,000+ locations across Asia) and instalment payment options — not Singapore-focused SMBs seeking fast onboarding. 2C2P’s differentiator is its physical payment network across Asia and its instalment processing capability. For a Jurong East retailer focused on accepting Visa and PayNow from local customers, this infrastructure adds complexity without direct benefit. PayPal Best for: Businesses selling to international customers who already hold PayPal accounts — particularly cross-border e-commerce with buyers in the US, Europe, or Australia. PayPal’s 400 million active global accounts make it relevant for export-facing e-commerce. For domestic Singapore transactions, it lacks PayNow and GrabPay, and its consumer-facing fee structure is less competitive for high-volume local retail. Fiuu Best for: Businesses that need virtual terminal card acceptance via mobile phone with minimal hardware — a specific use case where Fiuu ‘s virtual terminal capability is relevant. Fiuu (formerly Razer Merchant Services) supports card acceptance in Singapore. Its local e-wallet coverage for Singapore is limited compared to HitPay. Pricing is not publicly disclosed at the transaction level. What should Singapore SMBs prioritise when choosing a card gateway? For most Singapore SMBs, the decision comes down to four criteria: Card breadth — Visa, Mastercard, Amex, UnionPay, Apple Pay, and Google Pay covered in a single integration. Local method coverage — PayNow, GrabPay, and ShopeePay at minimum. BNPL (Atome, ShopBack PayLater) for retail. Payout speed — next business day SGD settlement for card revenue. Fee structure — no monthly fees for businesses under $50K/month in card volume. The article on lowering payment processing fees in Singapore covers practical strategies for reducing card transaction costs at the operational level. Frequently Asked Questions What is the best payment gateway for card payments in Singapore? HitPay is the most comprehensive option for Singapore SMBs that need card payments (Visa, Mastercard, Amex, UnionPay, Apple Pay, Google Pay) alongside PayNow, GrabPay, and ShopeePay — with no monthly fees and next business day SGD payouts. Stripe is a strong alternative for developer-led teams, and Adyen suits enterprise-scale operations with high transaction volumes. Does HitPay support card payments in Singapore? HitPay supports Visa, Mastercard, Amex, UnionPay, Apple Pay, and Google Pay in Singapore. HitPay is MAS-licensed (PS20200643), charges no monthly or setup fees, and settles card transactions the next business day in SGD. Transaction rates are available at hitpayapp.com/pricing. Is Stripe or HitPay better for a Singapore small business accepting card payments? Both Stripe and HitPay accept Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayNow, and GrabPay in Singapore with no monthly fees. HitPay adds ShopeePay, Atome, ShopBack PayLater, and cross-border wallets (WeChat Pay, UPI, QRIS, PromptPay) that Stripe does not support in Singapore — making HitPay the broader solution for SMBs serving mixed domestic and tourist customer bases. Stripe is better suited to developer teams building custom payment flows. How long does it take to get approved for a Singapore payment gateway? HitPay approves Singapore merchants in 1–3 business days with no setup fee. Approval timelines for Stripe are typically similar. Adyen and Airwallex’s enterprise-oriented onboarding can take significantly longer and may involve minimum volume commitments. What card payment gateways are licensed by MAS in Singapore? HitPay (PS20200643), Stripe, Adyen, Airwallex, 2C2P, and PayPal all operate as licensed or regulated entities in Singapore under the Payment Services Act 2019, overseen by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS). Merchants should verify any gateway’s licence status directly on the MAS public register before onboarding. Does accepting card payments in Singapore require a physical terminal? No. Singapore merchants can accept card payments without a physical terminal using payment links, online checkout, or Tap to Pay on iPhone — all supported by HitPay. Physical card readers are optional for in-person retail but not required for e-commerce, social commerce, or invoice-based businesses. What cross-border payment methods can Singapore card gateway merchants accept? Singapore merchants on HitPay can accept payments from international visitors using WeChat Pay (China), UPI (India), QRIS (Indonesia), PromptPay and LINE Pay (Thailand), DuitNow (Malaysia), QR Ph (Philippines), and and select South Korean wallets — without currency exchange at the point of sale. Cross-border transactions settle at T+2 in SGD.

title: Nestle Internship 2027–2028: Programs, Deadlines & How to Apply
summary: Everything you need to land a Nestle internship in 2027–2028, the 10+ tracks from Sales to R&D, expected deadlines, the multi-stage interview process, and tips to stand out at the world's largest food company.
body_text: Nestle Internship 2027–2028: Programs, Deadlines & How to Apply Last updated: July 2026 Nestlé is the world's largest food and beverage company , CHF 89.5 billion in revenue, over 2,000 brands across 188 countries, and 36,000 employees in the US alone. Its summer internship program places students into 10-week paid rotations across Sales, Marketing, Finance, Supply Chain, Engineering, IT, R&D, and more, each one feeding directly into a corresponding full-time development program. The 2027 Sales Internship is already live at $23.50/hr with no posted closing date, and remaining tracks are expected to follow by October 2026. That makes Nestlé one of the earliest-opening CPG summer programs for summer 2027, and rolling review means the class starts filling the moment a posting goes up. Quick Facts Fact Detail Where to apply nestlejobs.com early careers . Join the Talent Community for opening alerts Application window (2027) Sales already open (July 2026); remaining tracks expected August–October 2026 for summer 2027 Rolling? Yes. No hard closing dates posted; applications reviewed as they arrive Eligibility Pursuing a Bachelor's in a related field (graduating by June 2028 for the 2027 cycle); must be authorized to work in the US Duration 10–12 weeks (summer) Compensation $23.50/hr (2027 Sales JD); Indeed average across Nestlé interns is $23.22/hr Return offers No published rate; internships "feed directly into" full-time development programs Locations Arlington VA, Solon OH, St. Louis MO, Nashville, Tampa, Seattle, and 25+ factory sites # Programs 10+ tracks: Sales, Marketing, Finance, Supply Chain, Engineering, IT, R&D, HR, Legal, PR, and more The headline: Nestlé's 2027 Sales Internship is already accepting applications at $23.50/hr, with the remaining tracks expected August through October 2026. Review is rolling, there is no hard closing date, and the online assessments alone screen out 50 to 80 percent of applicants. Externships are short, remote professional experience programs where you finish a real project with a real company. The Beats by Dre Consumer Behavior & Market Analysis Externship and the Beats by Dre Data Analytics Externship build exactly the consumer-insight and analytical evidence a CPG application needs. Explore all Externships . What Is a Nestlé Internship? A Nestlé internship is a paid, 10-to-12-week summer placement that puts college students into real functional roles, Sales, Marketing, Finance, Supply Chain, Engineering, IT, R&D, HR, Legal, and PR, across Nestlé's US operating companies, from Nestlé USA in Arlington to Nestlé Purina PetCare in St. Louis to factory sites in 28 states. Intern reviews back the program up: 4.1 out of 5 on Glassdoor with a 4.7 for Culture & Values and a 4.4 for Diversity & Inclusion. And each track connects to a named full-time pipeline: finish the Sales internship well, and you're positioned for the Sales Development Program; finish Engineering, and the Factory Management Development track opens. The program is designed as an audition, not a summer job. When Do Nestlé Internship Applications Open for 2027–2028? Nestlé's US internship calendar starts earlier than most CPG peers. The 2027 Sales Internship went live in July 2026, and based on prior cycles the remaining tracks (Finance, Marketing, Supply Chain, Engineering, IT, R&D) are expected to post between August and October 2026. Review is rolling throughout, with no hard closing dates on most postings. The full process averages about 32 days on Glassdoor , but the online assessment stage alone eliminates 50 to 80 percent of applicants , so the real filter hits before the interview even starts. Now · Summer 2026 you're HERE The 2027 Sales Internship is already live and accepting applications at $23.50/hr. Remaining 2027 tracks have not yet posted. This is the window to build proof and apply to Sales immediately if that's your track. The Beats by Dre Consumer Behavior & Market Analysis Externship and the Beats by Dre Data Analytics Externship are remote, real-company projects that give an application finished consumer-insight work to point at. August to October 2026 EXPECTED ROLLING — APPLY WEEK 1 Remaining 2027 tracks (Finance, Marketing, Supply Chain, Engineering, IT, R&D, HR) expected to post here based on prior-cycle pattern. Rolling review means week-one applications meet the most open seats. November 2026 to March 2027 EXPECTED Online assessments (Cappfinity situational judgment, reasoning tests, or game-based evaluations), HireVue video interview, recruiter call, and hiring manager behavioral rounds. Expect offers between January and March. Summer 2027 10 to 12 weeks, May or June start, across Nestlé's US sites. Perform well: each internship track feeds directly into a named full-time development program. August to October 2027 EXPECTED Summer 2028 postings expected to begin, following the same late-summer/early-fall pattern. Apply within the first two weeks of each posting going live. Why You Must Apply the Week Applications Open Nestlé doesn't post closing dates on most internship listings, and GraduatesFirst confirms that applications are reviewed on a rolling basis: "Apply as early as possible as applications are on a rolling basis and this will give you a head start." But the real urgency is what happens after you apply. The online assessment stage eliminates 50 to 80 percent of the candidate pool, and the candidates who clear it enter a HireVue and behavioral interview pipeline that fills seats as it goes. By the time a late applicant submits, the seats they are competing for may already have offers attached. The 2027 Sales posting went up in July 2026 with no deadline. That isn't an open invitation to wait. that's a rolling class filling in real time. Which Nestlé Internship Programs Should You Target? Nestlé runs 10-plus internship tracks across its US operating companies, each feeding into a corresponding full-time development program. The function you pick determines your location, your assessment, and your conversion path. Track Focus Duration Key skills Sales Customer team partnerships, CPG category management, field experience 10 weeks Analytical skills, Excel, PowerPoint, initiative Marketing / Brand Management (MBA) Brand strategy, campaigns, consumer insights, product launches 10 weeks Strategic thinking, analytics, consumer research Finance & Accounting Financial planning, factory finance, audit, corporate FP&A 10–12 weeks Accounting coursework, Excel, financial modeling Supply Chain Forecasting, logistics, production planning, distribution 10–12 weeks Analytics, ERP/SAP, operations management Engineering Capital projects, automation, new technologies, infrastructure 10–12 weeks ME/ChE/IE/EE degree, design, project management IT & Digital App development, data analytics, cybersecurity, digital transformation 10–12 weeks CS/STEM, Python, SQL, cloud platforms See the full list of tracks on the Nestlé early careers page , which also covers R&D, Human Resources, Legal (1L), Public Relations, and Retail Operations. Each track maps to a named full-time development program: Sales Development, Finance Management Trainee, Factory Management Development, Supply Chain Development, and Marketing Development, among others. What Are the Eligibility Requirements? Nestlé's requirements, drawn from the 2027 Sales Internship JD and the early careers page: • Enrollment: currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in a related field, with graduation expected by June 2028 (for the summer 2027 cycle). MBA first-years are eligible for Marketing. • GPA: preferred cumulative GPA of 3.0 or above. Phrased as "preferred" in the Sales JD, not a hard cutoff. • Work authorization: must be authorized to work in the US. CPT/OPT (school-authorized) typically qualifies. H-1B sponsorship for post-internship full-time roles varies by division. • Leadership: leadership experience "through, but not limited to, an extra-curricular activity, organization, club, sports team, or employment" is explicitly required in the Sales JD. • Relocation: must be willing to relocate to the assigned intern location for the full program, and willing to relocate for a full-time role if extended an offer. Is Nestlé's 3.0 GPA Requirement a Hard Cutoff? Not quite. The 2027 Sales JD phrases it as a "preferred cumulative GPA of 3.0 or above," which is deliberate language: preferred, not required. That said, the online assessment stage is the real filter, it eliminates 50 to 80 percent of applicants regardless of GPA. So a 2.9 with strong leadership and assessment prep has a real shot, while a 3.8 who doesn't practice situational judgment tests will likely wash out at the same stage everyone else does. What Skills Does Nestlé Look For, and How Do You Build Them? Read across Nestlé's available 2026–2027 cycle postings, the full Sales JD, MBA Marketing, Finance references, and the early-careers page descriptions, and a clear pattern emerges. Analytical skills and communication appear across every track. Leadership and initiative show up in every posting that lists behavioral requirements. But the skill Nestlé calls out that most CPG peers don't is product enthusiasm: the Sales JD explicitly asks candidates to be "willing to generate enthusiasm and excitement for our products." that's a tell. Nestlé interviews for brand believers, not just competent analysts. What Nestlé looks for in interns Skills across 4 Nestlé intern & analyst job descriptions · 2026–27 cycle Nestlé intern postings (Sales, Marketing, Finance, IT), projecting 2027–2028 Analytical skills 4 of 4 Communication (written & verbal) 4 of 4 Leadership & initiative 4 of 4 Teamwork & collaboration 3 of 4 Excel & data analysis 3 of 4 Adaptability & fast learning 3 of 4 Attention to detail 2 of 4 Product & brand enthusiasm 2 of 4 Method: full-text analysis of Nestlé's 2027 Sales Internship JD, 2026 MBA Marketing posting, Finance and IT track descriptions, and early-careers page requirements. Prior-cycle basis; leadership and initiative are assessed behaviorally rather than listed as hard qualifications in every posting. How Is Demand for CPG and Marketing Interns Moving Right Now? CPG and marketing intern hiring right now: July 2026 Across US CPG, marketing, and supply-chain intern postings tracked this month · aggregate market signals, all employers = Summer intern boards are in their quiet season: CPG and marketing intern postings hold at a low mid-summer baseline, with the next wave expected as fall campus recruiting opens in August and September ★ Data skills are colonizing CPG JDs: SQL, Python, and dashboarding requirements now appear in supply-chain and brand-management intern postings, not just analytics-specific roles ▲ The bench you convert into is deep: brand management, supply chain analyst, and marketing associate roles remain among the most consistently posted entry-level positions at large CPG employers July 2026 is this tracker's baseline month, so month-over-month shifts appear at the August update. The signal now is seasonal: CPG intern demand is paused, not falling, and the data-skilled end of the market keeps growing. Method: qualitative scan of US CPG, marketing-intern, and supply-chain-intern postings across major job boards, July 2026 baseline. Figures show direction and relative level, not total market share. Build These Skills Before You Apply And every skill in that chart maps to a remote Externship where you finish a real company project before the application window closes. Skill (from real JDs) JD evidence Externship that builds it Consumer insight & analytical storytelling Sales JD: "excellent analytical skills"; Marketing: "consumer insights, product launches" Beats by Dre Consumer Behavior & Market Analysis Data analysis & reporting IT JD: Python, SQL, data analytics; Supply Chain: forecasting and distribution optimization Beats by Dre Data Analytics Operations & supply chain strategy Supply Chain JD: logistics, production planning, distribution; Engineering: capital projects and automation Amazon Fulfillment Center Operations Strategy How close is the overlap? The Beats consumer-behavior project ends on a consumer-insight presentation a Marketing interviewer can walk through slide by slide, and the Amazon operations deliverable yields the process-analysis story a Supply Chain behavioral round wants. What Is the Nestlé Application and Interview Process Like? Nestlé's hiring funnel is longer and more structured than most CPG peers, averaging about 32 days with a multi-stage assessment filter: 1. Apply at nestlejobs.com or through the AI Job Assistant "Olivia." Upload a resume, provide education and experience details, and select your preferred track. You can also apply via LinkedIn. Budget about 25 to 30 minutes. 2. Online assessment tests. If your application advances, you receive an invitation to complete assessments developed by Cappfinity, situational judgment, logical reasoning, numerical reasoning, and verbal reasoning tests, plus game-based evaluations on some tracks. This stage eliminates 50 to 80 percent of applicants . 3. HireVue on-demand video interview. About 7 pre-recorded questions testing motivation, skills, and alignment with Nestlé's core values. Basic prompts include "Why this role?" and "Why Nestlé?" plus STAR-format behavioral scenarios. 4. Recruiter call and hiring manager interview. A 20-to-30-minute recruiter conversation, then a behavioral round with the hiring manager (20 to 25 minutes). Some tracks add a Super Day at headquarters: three back-to-back 30-minute panel interviews. 5. Offer. Offers typically arrive between January and March, with onboarding details following. The full process averages about 32 days from application to decision. The bottleneck is stage two. Most candidates never reach the video interview, which means assessment prep is worth more than resume polish. Practice situational judgment and numerical reasoning tests before applying. And if you're facing a HireVue round, our HireVue question guide with a free AI mock tool runs the same format and time pressure. What Students on Reddit Say Three threads show how the process and culture play out from the inside. Got an email from a recruiter to schedule a 20-to-30-minute call to discuss their openings and my experience. Is this standard, or did I get lucky? It felt out of the blue after I applied weeks ago. r/internships applicant question, paraphrased · read the thread My boss used to work for Nestlé and they only have bad things to say about upper management. But other people say it depends entirely on your team and location. I think that's true of any company this size. r/supplychain workplace culture thread, paraphrased · read the thread I was selected for an internship at Nestlé in marketing. I loved everything about it for about four months. The intern experience was curated and exciting, but the full-time role felt different from day one. r/jobs intern-to-FT reflection, paraphrased · read the thread How Do You Stand Out When the Assessment Cuts 80 Percent? Three moves, all executable before the posting closes. First, apply within two weeks of any track going live; rolling review plus no posted deadlines means the class fills while you're still polishing your resume. Second, prepare for the online assessments like they are the real interview, because they are: situational judgment, numerical reasoning, and logical reasoning tests screen out the majority of candidates before anyone reads your application. Practice with Cappfinity-style tests and the Predictive Index cognitive format. Third, bring product enthusiasm backed by evidence. Nestlé explicitly values candidates who can "generate enthusiasm and excitement for our products," and a finished consumer-insight or data-analytics project answers that with portfolio proof instead of a talking point. And remember: each internship track connects to a named full-time development program. Interview like someone auditioning for the return offer, because you're. What Other Companies Should You Consider? Nestlé's peer set in CPG splits by what you want: brand-marketing training grounds, supply-chain powerhouses, or companies with similar rolling fall windows. P&G the classic brand-management training ground; similar assessment-first process and fall window Guide → Unilever Nestlé's closest global CPG rival; strong sustainability brand and similar functional tracks Careers site General Mills Minneapolis-based food company with a structured campus recruiting cycle and behavioral interviews Careers site PepsiCo food and beverage giant with a large summer program and strong supply-chain track Careers site Our P&G internship guide maps Nestlé's closest CPG peer in the same depth. FAQ When do Nestle internship applications open for summer 2027? They have already started. The 2027 Sales Internship posted in July 2026 with no closing date. Remaining tracks, Finance, Marketing, Supply Chain, Engineering, IT, R&D, and others, are expected to post between August and October 2026, based on prior-cycle timing. Join the Nestlé Early Careers Talent Community at nestlejobs.com for alerts. Is Nestle's internship application process rolling? Yes, effectively. Nestlé doesn't list hard closing dates on most internship postings, and prep guides confirm applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. The 2027 Sales JD had no posted deadline. Apply within the first two weeks of any posting going live. What GPA do I need for a Nestle internship? The 2027 Sales Internship lists a "preferred cumulative GPA of 3.0 or above." Preferred, not required, so a 2.9 with strong leadership or assessment performance has a real shot. But the online assessments are the real gate: they eliminate 50 to 80 percent of applicants before the interview stage. What is the Nestle internship interview process like? After applying, qualifying candidates take online assessments (situational judgment, reasoning tests, or game-based evaluations) that screen out 50 to 80 percent of applicants. Survivors proceed to a HireVue on-demand video interview with about 7 questions. Next is a 20-to-30-minute recruiter call, then a behavioral interview with the hiring manager. Some tracks add a Super Day with three back-to-back panel interviews. The full process averages about 32 days. How much does a Nestle internship pay? The 2027 Sales Internship starts at $23.50 per hour. Indeed estimates the average Nestlé intern rate at $23.22 per hour, which is 16 percent above the national intern average. Glassdoor pegs the range at $42K to $70K annualized depending on the track and division. Data science and IT interns may earn slightly more at $24 to $25 per hour. Do Nestle interns get return offers? Nestlé doesn't publish a specific conversion rate, but the company says internships "feed directly into" full-time development programs and high performers "may receive a full-time offer." Multiple former interns on the careers page describe converting to full-time. The NACE industry average for in-person internship offers is 72 percent, and Nestlé's structured pipeline design suggests rates at or above that benchmark. Does Nestle provide housing for interns? Nestlé provides relocation assistance and covers moving expenses for interns. Some programs include supplemented corporate housing, particularly for the first rotation of Management Development Programs. Specifics vary by track and location, so confirm with your recruiter after an offer. What skills does Nestle look for in interns? Across all tracks, Nestlé emphasizes analytical skills, communication, teamwork, initiative, and adaptability. The Sales JD specifically calls out Excel, PowerPoint, attention to detail, and comfort in fast-paced environments. Technical tracks add Python, SQL, and domain-specific tools. One differentiator: Nestlé explicitly values product enthusiasm, asking candidates to show they can generate excitement for the company's brands. Review is rolling, there is no posted deadline, and the online assessments cut the majority before anyone reaches the interview. Spend the runway building proof: a remote Externship turns "interested in CPG" into a finished consumer-insight or analytics project the application can point at. About the Author Bifei Wang has spent 17 years focused on human flow and the growth of young professionals, spanning international education, career training and coaching, and recruitment process outsourcing. Over 7 years at Extern, he has had one-on-one sessions with thousands of students exploring careers in consulting, finance, tech, marketing, and data, giving him a firsthand view of how the job market has shifted for early-career professionals and what it actually takes to break in.

title: Apache Ossie (Incubating): The New Name for Open Semantic Interchange
summary: Open Semantic Interchange is now Apache Ossie (Incubating) — a vendor-neutral semantic standard for AI and data tools, entering the Apache Incubator with 50+ contributors.
body_text: Apache Ossie is currently undergoing incubation at The Apache Software Foundation (ASF). If you've been following the Open Semantic Interchange project, the open specification for semantic layer and ontology, there's an important update. The project has been accepted into the Apache Incubator under a new name: Apache Ossie (Incubating). The spec, the community and the mission haven't changed, but the name, governance home and long-term trajectory have. Why the new name? You may know this project as Open Semantic Interchange, or OSI. As the community prepared for incubation, the next step in the project's open source journey, they decided to rename the project "Ossie" to avoid confusion with other projects in the open source ecosystem that share the OSI acronym. The mascot is a kangaroo carrying semantic metadata in its pouch as it hops between systems in the data stack. Going forward: The project is Apache Ossie (Incubating) References to "OSI" as a project name are historical The specification and the YAML-based format for defining metrics, dimensions and relationships are unchanged If you've been building on Open Semantic Interchange, nothing breaks. The name changed, but the spec didn't. What is Ossie? Ossie is an open specification for both semantic layer and ontology. It defines a vendor-neutral format for expressing business metrics, dimensions and their relationships as well as broader business concepts and rules. It allows any tool — whether BI platforms, query engines or AI agents — to consume and produce semantic definitions without loss of meaning. The problem it solves is straightforward: The same business concept (say, "Monthly Active Users") is often defined inconsistently across an organization's CRM, data warehouse and BI tools. When a human analyst or an AI agent runs a query, they shouldn't have to guess which definition is correct. Ossie provides a shared, machine-readable format that encodes not just the data but the intent and business meaning behind it. Figure 1: Ossie-compliant semantic models are interoperable across data sources, AI agents, BI platforms and query engines. With Ossie, organizations can go beyond defining metrics to include broader business knowledge across data sources and tools. AI agents that calculate and make decisions based on these definitions get the full context a human analyst would have, not just raw numbers. Why the Apache Software Foundation (ASF)? Incubating Ossie with the Apache Software Foundation ensures that it remains an open standard with no single controlling entity. Given that the goal of Ossie is to provide industry-wide standardization of semantic data, ensuring that it has a vendor-neutral ground to operate in is crucial. Under incubation, Ossie operates with public mailing lists, GitHub-based development, a formal discussion-and-vote process for spec changes, and committership earned through contribution rather than employer affiliation. Note that as part of this transition, all mailing lists referring to Open Semantic Interchange will be retired; community members should use the ASF-provided project resources that are linked below instead. The community behind Ossie Ossie didn't start as a single-company project, and it already isn't governed as one. Since the repository opened in November 2025: More than 100 commits and 35 merged pull requests have landed from contributors at Snowflake, Salesforce, Databricks, dbt Labs, RelationalAI, GoodData and Honeydew The participating coalition has grown from 17 launch partners to more than 50 organizations Three working groups (Metric Language, Catalog and Ontology) operate with dedicated leads, meetings and public channels Reference implementations have been created, including the Ossie-to-dbt MetricFlow converter, Apache Polaris™ catalog metadata converter, and a Snowflake Semantic Model converter What's next Snowflake has been contributing to this project since its inception, and we'll continue as an active contributor to Ossie as it grows under ASF governance. The roadmap is not predetermined; all items will go through the same open discussion-and-vote process as everything else in the project. That said, there are a few areas we're excited about and hope to work with the community to contribute proposals for: Deepening the spec's expressiveness to accommodate what real enterprise models demand, including advanced metric logic, windowing functions and complex relationships Building converters for additional platforms and frameworks so that adopting Ossie doesn't require ripping out what you already have A standardized semantic query specification that any engine can support Integration with Apache Polaris so that semantic models are discoverable directly from the catalog Get involved Ossie is transitioning to ASF infrastructure as part of incubation. Watch for updates on the new project website , join the development mailing list, collaborate on GitHub and join the Ossie Slack workspace . Whether you're building an AI agent, BI tool or a query engine that needs to understand business context, Ossie is the community working to make sure you don't have to tackle semantic interoperability alone.

The Bottom Line Part 1. What Is Agentic Trading? Definition Agentic trading refers to AI systems capable of independently planning, reasoning, executing, and continuously refining trading decisions based on predefined investor objectives and risk parameters. What Makes Agentic Trading Different? Unlike traditional rule-based trading algorithms that execute predefined instructions, modern AI agents can analyze changing market conditions, reason through multiple scenarios, and adapt their strategies in real time. Rather than reacting to a single technical signal, agentic trading systems evaluate a broader set of information—including price movements, news events, macroeconomic trends, and portfolio exposure—to support more informed trading decisions. Core capabilities of agentic trading include: Interpret market events by analyzing earnings reports, economic releases, and breaking news Monitor multiple asset classes simultaneously , including stocks, ETFs, options, and other securities Prioritize trading opportunities based on predefined goals, market conditions, and risk tolerance Adjust strategies dynamically as volatility, liquidity, or market sentiment changes Execute trades within investor-defined constraints , such as position size, stop-loss levels, and portfolio allocation limits Agentic Trading vs Traditional Algorithmic Trading Feature Agentic Trading Traditional Algorithmic Trading Decision Making Adaptive Rule-based Market Analysis Multi-source AI reasoning Pre-programmed indicators Strategy Updates Continuous Manual Context Awareness High Limited Human Oversight Required Required Part 2. Investors should evaluate their financial goals, risk tolerance, and investment products before using AI-assisted trading tools. 4. Best Practices for Using Agentic Trading Tools AI-assisted trading tools work best when used as a support tool alongside investor judgment. To use agentic trading responsibly, investors should establish clear goals, understand potential risks, and remain involved throughout the decision-making process. Key practices include: Define investment objectives Set clear goals and align AI-assisted insights with your overall investment strategy, time horizon, and risk tolerance. Set risk limits Establish position-size limits, risk parameters, and trading guidelines before placing orders to help manage exposure. Review AI-generated insights Use AI analysis as a reference point and evaluate the information, assumptions, and potential risks before taking action. Monitor portfolio performance Regularly review trades, portfolio allocation, and market conditions to ensure decisions continue to align with your objectives. Maintain diversification and oversight Consider diversification across sectors and asset classes, while keeping human judgment involved in every investment decision. Part 4. FAQs 1. What is agentic stock trading? Agentic stock trading uses AI systems that analyze markets, plan strategies, and generate or execute trading actions within investor-defined rules. 2. Traditional algorithms follow fixed rules, while AI agentic trading can reason through changing market conditions and adapt strategies dynamically. 3. Is agentic trading legal in the United States?
